item.title: My Claude Code cron ran up $1,800 in two nights. The watchdog that stops it at $2
item.description: Four documented runaway agent bills ($1,818, $6,000, $437, $150), why per-call metrics hide the loop, and per-run/per-day caps with rv.

item.title: Claude Code Routine failed silently? How to know your scheduled agent actually ran
item.description: Green does not mean done. The 4 ways a scheduled Claude Code run fails with no error, and heartbeat plus evidence checks that catch each one.

item.title: The dead man's switch for AI agents (and why a ping isn't enough)
item.description: A ping monitor knows a job ran. For an agent that is the least interesting fact. What a dead man's switch has to check when the job is an LLM.

item.title: OpenClaw stuck in a polling loop: $150, a crash, and no alert. Detect it in 60 seconds
item.description: An OpenClaw agent called the same tool 1,535 times in two hours. Every call looked fine. How a retry-storm rule and a daily cap catch this before the bill.

item.title: 7 ways unattended AI agents fail silently, and one check for each
item.description: Seven ways a scheduled AI agent fails without an error, from a run that never starts to a run that does nothing, and the one detector that catches each.

item.title: Prove what your AI agent did: an audit trail for unattended agents
item.description: A real, tamper-evident proof of one agent run: hashed record, public daily Merkle chain, Bitcoin anchor. How to verify it with a stdlib script, and what it cannot prove.

item.title: Monitoring a headless claude -p job: hooks, exit codes, cost and alerts
item.description: A full tutorial for monitoring headless claude -p cron jobs with SessionStart, PostToolUse and Stop hooks: transcript cost, evidence checks and alerts.

item.title: Cronitor for AI agents: what changes when the job is an LLM
item.description: A cron monitor tells you the job ran. An AI agent also needs a cost cap, loop detection and an outcome check. What to keep and what to add.
